role: automatic tail nomination for fully announced active pairs, followed by bounded local physics
registration_context: announcement interface and eight manually stipulated advance-notice paths observed; automatic stock-interval nominations and their component outcomes remain unobserved

component_roster.state: retain each earlier_tail_nomination SOC and its two locked PN rows from saved_nomination_contexts; use its profile's original target fractions from saved_target_protocol
component_roster.fixture_announcements: two explicitly supplied signed announcements at the translated release/delivery clocks; each pair is a component fixture with no claim that its modified sign was the original public source sign
component_roster.own_execution: 30 minutes of current locked PN, first full pulse and nominated tail, then the second full pulse with both second-hour PN rows fixed at zero
component_roster.output: nomination inputs, scalar projection counts, command intervals, coupled allocation, stock at second call, continuous extrema and full-pulse physical feasibility; no minute traces

nomination_rule.access: own SOC, current PN, following first-call PN, original target fractions and released announcements only; select active deliveries at decision+30 and decision+90
nomination_rule.scope: this component rule requires both active calls already announced. An incomplete or inactive pair produces no active-pair command; no unreleased row is used to complete it
nomination_rule.projection_role: F is strictly decreasing in q. It includes the current pending half-hour, first ramp and hold, return to the newly nominated tail, and 28 idle minutes before the second call
nomination_rule.second_stock_band: with zero second-hour PN, next export needs [abs(peak)*31/60/eta_d,C]; next import needs [0,C-eta_c*abs(peak)*31/60]
nomination_rule.per_unit_intervals: intersect the second-stock band with attainable F([-98,98]). If empty, record infeasibility. Otherwise invert F at the band edges to obtain an allowed PN interval, clipped to [-98,98] MW
nomination_rule.original_target_preference: clip the original target_fraction*C to the feasible second-stock band and invert F to obtain the preferred command inside its PN interval
nomination_rule.inversion: reuse the two endpoint projections per unit; 48 bisection iterations per needed inverse. Lower command edge uses the bracket with F<=upper stock; upper command edge uses the bracket with F>=lower stock. Preferred command uses the bracket midpoint
nomination_rule.shared_power: choose each interval's command nearest zero. If their gross sum exceeds 98 MW, record coupled infeasibility. Otherwise move from this minimum command toward the preferred command with the largest common fraction whose gross sum fits 98 MW
nomination_rule.budget: at most 300 scalar F evaluations per nomination, at most one exact 150-minute trajectory per complete feasible probe; scalar projection calls are counted separately from physics
nomination_rule.failure_handling: retain missing announcements, empty stock bands, coupled infeasibility and physical failures as failed probes; no command retuning or replacement by the prior manual action table

component_checks: new-rule response to the second announced sign, absence of a command when the pair is not yet fully released, agreement of F with second-call stock from executed physics, and original physical tolerances. Record test calls separately
decision: after all eight complete safe probes, specify the remaining whole-hour and inactive-slot behavior and freeze a bounded announced-task pilot. A failed probe requires its exact mechanism before further controller work; no weekly rollout or matrix starts here
preservation: keep the original tasks, announcement interface and all prior results; write automatic nomination components separately
limitations: two saved initial states and supplied active sign pairs, with zero PN stipulated after the first hour; this is not a complete announced-task weekly policy, historical BM counterfactual, reliability estimate, source-benefit result or OR submission-readiness proof
